t.11.1: Arjuna said: By the supreme and secret word concerning the Self that you have spoken out of kindness to me, this delusion of mine has gone away.
t.11.2: For I have heard from you in detail, O lotus-eyed one, of the origin and dissolution of beings, and also of your imperishable greatness.
t.11.3: O Supreme Lord, it is just as you have described yourself. Yet I wish to see your divine, sovereign form, O Supreme Person.
t.11.4: O Lord, if you think that it can be seen by me, then, O Lord of Yoga, show me your imperishable Self.
t.11.5: The Blessed Lord said: Behold, O Pārtha, my forms by hundreds and by thousands, manifold and divine, of various colors and shapes.
t.11.6: Behold the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Aśvins, and likewise the Maruts; behold, O Bhārata, many wonders never seen before.
t.11.7: Behold now, O Guḍākeśa, the entire universe, with all that moves and does not move, standing here as one in my body, and whatever else you wish to see.
t.11.8: But you cannot see me with these eyes of your own. I give you divine sight; behold my sovereign yoga.
t.11.9: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus, O King, Hari, the great Lord of Yoga, then revealed to Pārtha his supreme, sovereign form.
t.11.10: A form with many mouths and eyes, presenting many wondrous sights, adorned with many divine ornaments, and holding many divine weapons raised aloft.
t.11.12: If the radiance of a thousand suns were to blaze forth all at once in the sky, that might resemble the radiance of that great-souled one.
t.11.11: Wearing celestial garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances, the God composed of all wonders, infinite, with faces turned in every direction.
t.11.13: There, in the body of the God of gods, the son of Pāṇḍu then beheld the entire universe, divided in many ways, gathered together in one place.
t.11.14: Then Dhanaṃjaya, filled with wonder, his hair standing on end, bowed his head to the god and, with joined palms, spoke.
t.11.16: I see You, of endless form on every side, with many arms, bellies, mouths and eyes. O Lord of the universe, O You whose form is the universe, I see no end of You, no middle, and again no beginning.
t.11.15: Arjuna said: O God, in your body I see all the gods and likewise the hosts of the various kinds of beings: Brahmā the lord seated on his lotus throne, all the sages, and the divine serpents.
t.11.17: I see You, crowned, bearing the mace and the discus, a mass of splendor blazing on every side, hard to behold all around, radiant like the burning fire and the sun, immeasurable.
t.11.18: You are the Imperishable, the Supreme, the one to be known; you are the supreme resting place of this universe. You are the unchanging guardian of eternal dharma; you are the everlasting Puruṣa, so I believe.
t.11.19: I see You without beginning, middle, or end, of infinite power, with countless arms, the moon and sun as Your eyes, Your mouth a blazing fire, scorching this whole universe with Your own radiance.
t.11.20: This space between heaven and earth, and all the directions, are pervaded by you alone. Seeing this wondrous and terrible form of yours, the three worlds tremble, O great-souled one.
t.11.21: These hosts of gods enter into you; some, afraid, praise you with joined palms. Saying "May it be well!", the hosts of great seers and Siddhas praise you with abundant hymns.
t.11.22: The Rudras, Ādityas and Vasus, and those who are the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, the two Aśvins, the Maruts and the Ūṣmapas, and the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras and Siddhas all gaze upon you, utterly amazed.
t.11.23: Seeing your immense form, O mighty-armed one, with many mouths and eyes, with many arms, thighs and feet, with many bellies, terrible with many tusks, the worlds are shaken, and so am I.
t.11.24: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing, of many colors, with mouths wide open and vast flaming eyes, my inmost self is shaken with fear, and I find neither steadiness nor peace, O Viṣṇu.
t.11.25: Having merely seen your mouths, terrible with tusks and resembling the fire of time's end, I know not the directions and find no refuge; be gracious, Lord of the gods, abode of the world!
t.11.27: Rushing, they enter your fearsome mouths, terrible with tusks; some are seen caught between your teeth, their heads crushed to powder.
t.11.26: And all these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with the hosts of the rulers of the earth, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and likewise that son of the charioteer, along with the foremost warriors of our own side as well, are rushing toward you.
t.11.28: As the many torrents of the rivers rush headlong toward the ocean alone, so do these heroes of the world of men enter your mouths, blazing all around.
t.11.29: As moths rush with swift speed into a blazing fire to their destruction, so too do the worlds rush with swift speed into your mouths to their destruction.
t.11.30: Devouring all the worlds on every side with your flaming mouths, you lick them up again and again; filling the whole universe with brilliance, your fierce rays blaze forth and scorch it, O Viṣṇu.
t.11.31: Tell me who you are, you of terrible form; salutation be to you, O best of gods, be gracious! I wish to know you, the primal one, for I do not understand your course of action.
t.11.32: The Blessed Lord said: I am Time, the mighty destroyer of the worlds, set forth here to annihilate the worlds. Even without you, all these warriors arrayed in the opposing ranks shall cease to be.
t.11.33: Therefore stand up and win glory; having conquered your enemies, enjoy a prosperous kingdom. By me alone these have already been slain; be merely the instrument, O Savyasācin.
t.11.34: Droṇa and Bhīṣma and Jayadratha and Karṇa, and likewise the other heroic warriors, already slain by me, do you slay; do not be distressed. Fight, and you will conquer your rivals in battle.
t.11.35: Sañjaya said: Having heard these words of Keśava, the crowned one, trembling, with joined palms, made obeisance, and bowing down again, utterly terrified, spoke to Kṛṣṇa in a faltering voice.
t.11.36: Arjuna said: Rightly, O Hṛṣīkeśa, does the world rejoice and delight in your praise; the terrified Rākṣasas flee in all directions, and all the hosts of the Siddhas bow down to you.
t.11.37: And why should they not bow down to you, O Great Soul, who are greater even than Brahmā, to you, the original creator? O Infinite One, Lord of the gods, Abode of the universe, you are the imperishable, being and non-being, and that which is beyond both.
t.11.39: You are Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the moon, Prajāpati, and the great-grandfather. Salutations, salutations to You a thousand times, and again and yet again, salutations, salutations to You!
t.11.38: You are the primal God, the ancient Person; you are the supreme resting place of this universe. You are the knower of what is to be known and of the supreme abode; by you this universe is pervaded, O you of infinite form.
t.11.40: Salutation to you in front and also behind; let salutation be to you on every side, O All! You are of infinite valor and immeasurable might; you pervade all, and therefore you are all.
t.11.42: And if, for the sake of jest, you were treated with disrespect while at play, resting, sitting, or eating, whether alone or in the presence of others, O Acyuta, for that I beg forgiveness of you, the immeasurable one.
t.11.41: Whatever I have said rashly, thinking of you as a friend, calling out 'O Kṛṣṇa, O Yādava, O friend,' not knowing this greatness of yours, whether out of carelessness or even out of affection...
t.11.43: You are the father of this world, of all that moves and does not move; you are its object of worship and its most venerable teacher. There is none equal to you; how then could there be another greater than you, even in the three worlds, O you of incomparable power?
t.11.44: Therefore, bowing down and prostrating my body, I seek your grace, O Lord worthy of praise. As a father bears with his son, as a friend with his friend, as a lover with the beloved, so you should bear with me, O God.
t.11.46: I wish to see you just as before, wearing a crown, bearing a mace, with the discus in hand. O thousand-armed one, O you whose form is the universe, become that very four-armed form.
t.11.47: The Blessed Lord said: Arjuna, out of my grace I have, by my own yogic power, shown you this supreme form, radiant, universal, infinite and primal, this form of mine that no one other than you has ever seen before.
t.11.45: Having seen what was never seen before, I am thrilled, and yet my mind is shaken with fear. Show me, O God, that very form of yours; be gracious, O Lord of the gods, O abode of the universe!
t.11.48: Neither by the Vedas, sacrifices and study, nor by gifts, nor by rituals, nor by severe austerities can I in this form be seen in the world of men by anyone other than you, O great hero of the Kurus.
t.11.49: Let there be no distress for you, nor a state of bewilderment, at having seen this terrible form of mine. Free from fear and with a gladdened mind, behold once again that very form of mine.
t.11.50: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus to Arjuna, Vāsudeva again revealed his own form; and the great-souled one, becoming once more gentle in form, consoled him who was terrified.
t.11.51: Arjuna said: Seeing this gentle human form of yours, O Janārdana, I have now become composed in mind and have returned to my normal nature.
t.11.52: The Blessed Lord said: This form of mine that you have seen is very hard to behold; even the gods are ever longing for a sight of this form.
t.11.53: Not by the Vedas, nor by austerity, nor by charity, nor by sacrifice can I be seen in this form, as you have seen me.
t.11.54: But only by undivided devotion, O Arjuna, can I in this form be known, and truly seen, and entered into, O scorcher of foes.
t.11.55: He who does work for me, who holds me as the supreme goal, who is devoted to me, free from attachment, and without enmity toward any being, he comes to me, O Pāṇḍava.
